                                                                             the human hand is not just desirable, it is essential.
Imagine a high-stakes environment like robot-assisted surgery,               Vision Language Models (VLMs) have rapidly become the per-
where a subtle misinterpretation of a surgeon’s hand gesture                 ceptual and decision-making core of embodied agents, AR/VR
whether a finger is slightly bent or fully extended can mean                 platforms, and multimodal assistants due to their ability to unify
the difference between a successful operation and a critical er-             visual perception and natural-language reasoning within a single
ror [19, 41]. Or consider chip manufacturing, where robotic                  foundation model [42]. As these systems increasingly rely on
agents mimic human motions with microscopic precision, and                   such unified reasoning, fine-grained hand-pose understanding
a misjudged fingertip angle can cause costly defects [17, 53]. In            becomes crucial [4, 59]. Hands are often the primary medium

Figure 2. Overview of HandVQA Question Format. This figure illustrates the structure of our benchmark, which divides hand pose estimation
into five sub-tasks: Angle, Distance, and Relative Position along X, Y, and Z axes. A hand image with annotated joint indices (top left) supports
multiple-choice questions per task type, derived from 3D joint coordinates and the correct answers are shown in green.

2. Related Works                                                             are grounded in the real 3D coordinates, we test the model’s abil-
Hallucinations and Alignment Failures in VLMs. Vision-                       ity to grasp Euclidean spatial concepts like distance and angle.
language models (VLMs) often suffer from hallucinations,                     VQA Benchmarks and Fine-Grained Reasoning Evaluation.
i.e., generating content not grounded in the image; such                     The VQA field has progressed from basic object/attribute
as nonexistent objects, incorrect attributes, or false spatial               Q&A (e.g., VQAv1/v2) [2] to compositional and fine-grained
relations [38]. For example, a model might describe a ring                   reasoning tasks. CLEVR [26] introduced logical queries in syn-
that isn’t there or misstate left/right positions [27, 33]. Even             thetic scenes; GQA [22] used real images and scene graphs for
state-of-the-art models like GPT-4V [1] and BLIP-2 [32]                      multi-step reasoning. Recent benchmarks like A-OKVQA [50]
hallucinate objects [33], struggle with spatial terms [27], or               and Encyclopedic-VQA [43] test domain knowledge, but fine-
fabricate colors and shapes [25]. These issues stem from weak                grained accuracy remains low: e.g., PaLI [11] achieves only 13%
visual-textual alignment and overreliance on language priors                 on Encyclopedic-VQA [43]. Our benchmark instead focuses
[24, 57, 62]. Liu et al. [35] emphasizes the lack of grounding               on fine-grained spatial understanding. It aligns with works like
signals in training data. Recent solutions include evaluation                NLVR2 [54] and CLEVR-3D [60] that emphasize logical con-
frameworks such as POPE [33], NOPE [39], and Hal-Eval [25],                  sistency and physical reasoning. Recent diagnostic frameworks
as well as mitigation strategies, including contrastive decoding,            such as VERIFY [5] evaluate if models follow reasoning chains
reinforcement learning [8], and robust visual encoders [36].                 rather than shallow cues. II-MMR [29] categorizes multi-hop

Figure 3. Overview of the HandVQA pipeline. The pipeline converts normalized 3D hand joints into interpretable VQA pairs through three deter-
ministic stages: (1) Fpose computes continuous pose descriptors: angles (θ), distances (d), and relative positions (Δx ,Δy ,Δz ) and categorizes them
into discrete pose descriptors (Γ); (2) Ftext fills deterministic sentence templates using Γ and filters correct and incorrect options to form candidate an-
swer options (O) and the correct label y ; (3) Fmcq constructs multiple-choice questions (MCQ) by pairing each image with O and its correct label y .


questions multiple-choice and relatively constrained—allowing                    Interaction. By forcing models to reason about joint-level spatial
clean assessment of spatial reasoning accuracy. It thus adds to                  details, HandVQA not only evaluates but actively improves mul-
diagnostic tools assessing whether progress in general VQA                       timodal perception and grounding for these critical applications.
translates to true fine-grained understanding.

3.2. Sentence Generation (Ftext )                                                       relative positions along the X, Y, and Z axes. For angle and dis-
                                                                                        tance, we report both accuracy and mean absolute error (MAE).
Given discrete pose descriptors Γ, the sentence generation step                         While accuracy captures correct predictions, MAE reflects
first fills deterministic templates with joint names and category                       the average deviation from ground truth—crucial for ordinal
labels to create natural language sentences S = {s1,s2,...,sn}.                         categories where not all errors are equally severe (e.g., misclas-
Each descriptor type uses a fixed syntactic structure. For                              sifying “bent completely inward” joint as “straight” is worse
instance, the template for a distance descriptor is:                                    than as “bent inward”). To compute MAE, we assign ordinal
             “The {joint A} joint of the {finger A} is                                  indices to each category based on increasing magnitude. For the
              {category label} the {joint B} joint of the {finger B}.”                  angle task, the four categories—bent completely inward, bent
                                                                                        inward, bent slightly inward, and straight—are mapped to class
If the category label is “close to,” the resulting sentence                             indices 0, 1, 2, and 3, respectively, reflecting increasing joint
becomes: “The distal interphalangeal joint of the middle finger                         angles. For the distance task, the categories—close to, spread
is close to the distal interphalangeal joint of the ring finger.”                       from, and spread wide from—are assigned indices 0, 1, and 2,
From the full set of generated sentences S, Ftext identifies the                        corresponding to increasing joint distances. For relative position

4.3. Zero-Shot Generalization to Novel Hand-
     Related Tasks                                                          HandVQA provides the first large-scale benchmark for
 Beyond diagnosing failures, we hypothesize that the 3D-                    diagnosing fine-grained 3D spatial reasoning about hands
 grounded spatial reasoning taught by HandVQA is a transferable             in VLMs. Our analyses reveal that current models, despite
 skill that should generalize to other novel, hand-related down-            strong general perception and instruction-following abilities,
 stream tasks. To test this transferable learning, we designed a            systematically fail on geometric relations such as joint angles,
 zero-shot generalization experiment, with results shown in Table           distances, and relative positions. By introducing a fully
4. We selected two distinct, novel tasks for evaluation: static             automated 3D-grounded annotation pipeline, we make these
 image-based Gesture recognition and video-based hand-object                failures explicit and measurable. Furthermore, our zero-shot
 Interaction recognition. For these experiments, we chose LLaVA             experiments show that HandVQA acts as an effective source
 Mistral 7B [34], best performing model in our benchmark and                of transferable 3D knowledge. Fine-tuning on our benchmark
 Qwen 2.5 VL 7B [3], given its support for temporal sequences               substantially improves performance on unseen tasks, such as
(required for the video-based interaction task). Following                  gesture recognition and hand–object interaction.
 common VLM finetuning practice [18, 37, 51, 56], we include                Future direction. As the first large-scale benchmark for fine-
 a small, domain-agnostic instruction-alignment set alongside               grained hand-centric spatial reasoning, HandVQA focuses on
 HandVQA (FreiHAND + InterHand2.6M + FPHA) to preserve                      core capabilities and naturally opens several research avenues:
 general instruction-following capabilities during training.                (i) Its discretized geometric representation offers a controlled
 Gesture Recognition. For this zero-shot task, we utilized                  and deterministic evaluation setup, with fixed thresholds
 the HaGRID dataset [28], which provides full-body images                   providing a simplified view of the continuous 3D space. Future
 annotated with 34 hand gestures (e.g., ‘taking picture’, ‘heart’,          work can develop adaptive or learned mappings that better
‘peace’, etc.). To adapt this dataset into a VLM-evaluable                  capture perceptual distinctions and support richer geometric
 format, we first convert each gesture label into a detailed                reasoning. (ii) The templated language ensures unambiguous
 natural-language description using Gemini [55]. Then, based                supervision, yet expanding to more diverse phrasing, compara-
 on these descriptions, we generate multiple-choice questions               tive expressions, and explanations could yield stronger linguistic
(MCQs) with one correct option and three carefully designed                 grounding of 3D geometry. (iii) Since the benchmark currently
 distractor options per sample. Following this process, we con-             targets static images, extending it to video would enable
 structed a final test set of 33,500 MCQs from the HaGRID test              reasoning about motion cues and contact dynamics central to
 split (Further details is available in supplemental.). As shown            many interaction tasks. (iv) Integrating HandVQA with Vision
 in Table 4, the base LLaVA and Qwen models achieve 57.42%                  Language Action (VLA) models offers a path toward improved

 curacies increase substantially to 69.58% (LLaVA) and 82.19%               We hope HandVQA facilitates the development of multimodal
